compatibilityPromise: Documented behavior is intentional and evidence-backed.
No execution target silently falls back.
Public surfaces may still change deliberately during beta before the stable 1.0.0 release.
Implementation and historical subpaths do not gain accidental compatibility guarantees.
Package names, release artifacts, and published versions remain immutable once released.

items.summary: Managed async handlers, Router/context behavior, sequential effects, keyed parallel effects, and terminal transfer agree across supported execution modes.
Structured projections, exact caller-owned bodies, opaque pass-through, and repeated headers retain bounded ownership across targets.
pulse.schema strict boundaries and semantic JSON codecs agree across Node and Fastly Native and JavaScript modes.
Config, secret, KV, fetch, GRIP, and logging observations preserve binding isolation and redact secret values.
Node Native, Node JavaScript, Fastly Native, and Fastly JavaScript produce matching semantic traces with explicit target-correct artifacts.
The canonical GRIP package root provides real JavaScript behavior and the trusted Native lowerer emits matching bounded operations.
items.verification: node wasm/scripts/run-wasm-tests.cjs --task package-reachability --task grip-package-owned-lowering --task grip-package-runtime --task grip-cross-target-conformance --no-report

items.summary: Inspection, eligibility, configured target, JavaScript source packages, and Native Wasm artifacts remain aligned without target masquerading.
The normal project workflow, output containment, provider truth, stable diagnostics, remediation, and exit policy match the documented contract.
Conformance and provider tests construct declared package-root dist outputs as owned transients and remove them explicitly after execution.
items.verification: Run the GRIP, four-mode, and Fastly JavaScript lanes from a source-only tree and verify packages/assets and packages/grip contain no dist or tsbuildinfo residue.

items.summary: Native ineligibility, provider failure, and explicit JavaScript selection remain fail-closed and never trigger automatic target fallback.
Arbitrary Promises, ambient asynchronous APIs, provider SDKs, streams, and background work remain outside Native eligibility.
items.reason: The Beta documents these forms as JavaScript-only or unsupported; widening the compiler is prohibited in 7D.

items.summary: Arbitrary third-party compiler-lowerer discovery and execution remain unsupported.
items.reason: Discovery, provenance, isolation, negotiation, and trust require a protected architecture decision.

items.summary: Pulse does not promise a standalone production Native Node launcher in the Beta.
items.reason: The maintained Node journey separates local execution from deployment-owner integration and does not overstate a production host adapter.

items.summary: Remote deployment, documentation promotion, npm publication, and Fastly activation are not authorized by local conformance.
items.reason: 7D proves supported behavior locally; packed candidates, external reality, and release authority belong to later checkpoints.

procedure: Generate and inspect an inert 0.0.0 tarball for each missing package name.
Publish each inert tarball with public access and the bootstrap dist-tag through a human 2FA-protected session.
Verify that every package name exists, bootstrap points to 0.0.0, and latest is either absent or still points to the same inert 0.0.0 bootstrap.
Configure the exact pulse-compute/pulse, npm-publish.yml, and npm-publish trusted-publisher identity on every package.
Revoke and remove the temporary bootstrap credential before the 1.0.0-beta.1 release candidate is published through OIDC.
Publish the synchronized 1.0.0-beta.1 candidate under beta only after protected human approval.

vulnerabilities.acceptance: No unresolved critical or high production advisory; every remaining production advisory has a release-owner disposition.

dependencyLicenses.reviewRequired: Any missing, custom, copyleft, source-available, or non-allowlisted production license requires an explicit human release disposition.
dependencyLicenses.noticeRule: Inspect NOTICE and attribution files for every production dependency whose material is bundled into a package or generated artifact; create and ship a root NOTICE only when redistribution obligations require it.

noticeDisposition.basis: Pulse Native schema artifacts compile AssemblyScript runtime code plus json-as and transitive xjb-as source into generated Wasm; their applicable notices and license attributions therefore travel with the release.

components.name: assemblyscript
components.relationship: Direct compiler runtime dependency and compiler/runtime material in generated Native artifacts.

components.name: json-as
components.relationship: Direct compiler runtime dependency whose schema-codec source is compiled into generated Native artifacts.

components.name: xjb-as
components.relationship: Transitive json-as dependency whose numeric formatting source is compiled into generated Native artifacts.

gates.summary: The intended public candidate is Pulse 1.0.0-beta.1 Beta under beta, never latest.
Apache-2.0 is selected and propagated to the root and all publishable manifests.
Supported Node is ^22.14.0 || ^24.0.0 and local development supports pnpm >=10 <11; reproducible publication uses Node 24.18.0, npm 11.15.0, and pnpm 10.0.0.
The release seal must restore the exact lockfile closure either directly or from the optional portable dependency bundle.
gates.nextAction: Run the release seal with a frozen install, --skip-install for an already verified closure, or --dependency-bundle for an offline restore.

gates.summary: The first-publication procedure reserves missing names with inert 0.0.0 packages under bootstrap before OIDC release publication.
Every manifest-owned package name must exist before publication; mutable registry observations are generated evidence and are not stored in this source policy.
gates.nextAction: Before publication, run npm run release:audit-npm, bootstrap every reported missing name, remediate any reported bootstrap/latest dist-tag drift through human authority, and rerun the audit within the configured freshness window.

gates.summary: Organization ownership, maintainers, enforced 2FA, recovery, and public package access are not verifiable from the source archive.
gates.nextAction: Record the npm organization owners, two independent recovery paths, 2FA policy, and package access after external verification.

gates.summary: The repository contract requires OIDC, but the trusted-publisher identity cannot be configured until package bootstrap completes.
gates.nextAction: Configure pulse-compute/pulse, npm-publish.yml, and npm-publish on every bootstrapped package and audit the settings.
gates.verification: Protected npm settings review for every manifest-owned package

gates.summary: The npm-publish environment contract exists in source, but repository environment protection is external state.
gates.nextAction: Verify release-tag restrictions and a human release-authority reviewer on the npm-publish environment.

gates.summary: Source metadata names pulse-compute/pulse, but public visibility, team access, rulesets, and release settings remain externally unverified.
gates.nextAction: Verify the canonical public repository identity and apply the repository setup checklist.

gates.summary: The source contract names https://pulsecompute.io with immutable /v1.0.0-beta.1 routes, but the final origin and Fastly route are not externally proven.
gates.nextAction: Verify origin ownership, immutable version routing, latest promotion, and the protected documentation-production environment.
gates.verification: Documentation origin and Fastly route review

gates.summary: The authoritative release seal requires real Fastly CLI execution; unavailable is not a passing state.
The Sprint 7D implementation ledger has zero release-blocking and zero unclassified conformance items.
The 1.0.0-beta.1 Beta snapshot is atomically aligned across release authority, documentation versions, package metadata, changelog, and generated references.
The final Fastly CLI version and its CLI-managed local Compute execution have not been recorded for the candidate.
gates.nextAction: Run fastly compute serve through the provider reality lane and record the Fastly CLI version; use an explicit Viceroy override only when diagnosing or reproducing that lower-level engine.

gates.summary: The production vulnerability command and severity disposition policy are fixed.
A 2026-07-25 preflight run reported 49 production dependencies and zero advisories; final evidence must be regenerated from the frozen candidate.
gates.nextAction: Rerun the production audit from the clean frozen checkout and record dispositions in the final release evidence.

gates.summary: Production license inventory, review, and NOTICE attribution rules are fixed.
The current production closure reports only MIT, Apache-2.0, and MIT AND Apache-2.0; the final packed and generated artifacts still require attribution review.
gates.nextAction: Regenerate the production license inventory from the frozen candidate and inspect all redistributed third-party material.

gates.summary: The release ships a root NOTICE for AssemblyScript, json-as, and xjb-as material compiled into generated Native artifacts, and every publishable tarball must carry the exact root legal files.
Every checked-in documentation source is deterministically classified and all deletion/supersession decisions are explicit.
